topic: MathKernel: Evidence-Aware Multi-Engine Mathematics MCP Server

key_points: Evidence-aware multi-engine mathematics runtime for LLMs; dual use as Python library (mathkernel) and MCP server (mathkernel-mcp)
Core principle: 'The LLM interprets intent; the MathKernel establishes mathematical evidence.' Inverts role so model parses/plans, kernel computes and records claim-specific evidence
Typed orchestration layer, not a single solver; facade owns parsing, contexts, identity, persistence, evidence composition, derivation tracking; domain adapters own actual math
Trust labels: exact, claim_evidence, symbolic, numeric, formal are distinct claims; exact arithmetic alone is not a formal proof; approximate-input ancestry must not silently disappear
Engines: exact, symbolic, formal/proof, certified-interval (rigorous enclosures), numeric, plus numba/CUDA/GPU (yolo) acceleration
162 MCP tools prefixed math_; FastMCP 3 over stdio; ships core instructions at initialize (discover->parse->context->trust discipline->async jobs->provenance)
Status Beta (development line), MIT license, created 2026-09-06; project has 'mathkernel' on PyPI at v1.3.0
Extra: mathkernel-viz, mathkernel-sonify, MathKernel Studio, skills packages
Symbolic Algebra MCP server exposing SymPy core functionality to LLMs for symbolic math / computer algebra
Single-engine (SymPy), ~79 stars, added Streamable HTTP transport in 2026
Run via uv or Docker (ghcr.io/sdiehl/sympy-mcp)
Advanced mathematical computation engine for LLMs; addresses LLM arithmetic errors in symbolic math, exact fractions, multi-step problems
3 tools, single compute gateway routes CAS-style strings; layers math.js (numeric) + Giac/Xcas WASM (symbolic)
Includes verify tool to check identity/solution/computation independently; stateless HTTP (POST /mcp), no session state
Benchmarks GLM-*; no auth yet, default bind 127.0.0.1, MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS for DNS-rebinding protection
MCP-Solver: bridges LLMs with symbolic/constraint solvers via MCP, an open standard
Demonstrates the pattern of coupling LLM intent to dedicated solver backends to avoid arithmetic errors and add rigor
Official MathWorks MATLAB MCP server; ~1,400 stars (renamed from matlab-mcp-core-server), high-traffic per PulseMCP
Runs MATLAB through AI agents in-conversation; broad client support (Claude Code/Desktop, VS Code, GitHub Copilot)
Represents the dominant incumbent: single heavy vendor platform vs MathKernel's lightweight multi-engine open approach
Market landscape: official MATLAB MCP server dominates; sdiehl/sympy-mcp growing; SageMath gap partially closed Apr 2026; symbolic math fragmentation easing
Covers MATLAB, SymPy, Wolfram, R, Julia, OpenFOAM, COMSOL across numerical/symbolic/statistical/HPC categories
Confirms multi-engine/evidence approach is differentiated vs single-engine symbolic or heavy vendor servers

angles: Evidence trust levels as the core differentiator: exact vs symbolic vs numeric vs formal are distinct claims — LLMs need provenance, not just answers
The intent/evidence division of labor: model interprets intent, kernel establishes evidence — fixes LLM arithmetic errors at the source
Multi-engine + cross-validation beats single-engine; error-rate reduction (12-18% -> <0.7%) is a compelling review hook
Open MIT multi-engine alternative vs the heavy single-vendor incumbents (MATLAB, Wolfram) in the 2026 math-MCP landscape
Practical evaluation: is 162-tool surface usable, or over-engineered for typical agent math needs?
Production caveats: Beta status, optional GPU/yolo mode is a safety gate not evidence, approximate-input ancestry constraints, no auth in some peers
